To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fine-grained high-Tc superconductors are characterized by the suppression of hole doping and by the appearance of pseudogap features even in samples with an oxygen content close to the optimum value.
the structural disorder of fine-grained HTS leads to a reduction in the level of doping and the creation (even in optimally doped samples) of the pseudogap features.
the structural disorder of YBa2Cu 3Oy superconductor with 〈D〉 <2 μm leads to suppression of hole doping and formation of features of pseudogap state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of structural defects on the properties of high-temperature superconducting (HTSC) YBa2Cu4Oy compounds.
the study of the effect of structural disordering of the crystal lattice inherent to fine-grain YBa2Cu 3Oy samples with different oxygen content y on the superconducting state.
the study of the effect of structural disordering on the properties of YBa2Cu 3Oy high-temperature superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fine-grained HTS YBa2Cu2Oy with an average grain size 〈D〉 <2 μm are characterized by a lower level of hole doping in the CuO2 layers than the bulk HTSC samples.
the structural disorder in the fine-grained HTS materials is a major cause of the suppression of the superconducting properties.

the structural disorder in fine-grained YBa2Cu2Oy samples with 〈D〉 < ∼ 2 μm leads to a suppression of hole doping and, hence, to an appearance of features inherent to pseudogap states even at y = 6.92.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suppression of hole doping is a universal effect in fine-grained YBa2Cu 3Oy samples with a 〈D〉 < ∼ 2 μm, regardless of the oxygen stoichiometry and the method of preparation.
the fine grained YBa2Cu4Oy is a pseudogap superconductor, while the coarse grained YBaCu4Oy with the grain size of 5-10 μm is a d-wave superconductor.

the structural disorder in YBa2Cu2O6+y superconductors with an average grain size 〈D〉 < ∼2 μm leads to the suppression of the level of the hole doping and the emergence of features inherent to pseudogap state.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structural disorder- ing inherent to fine-grain HTSC YBaCuOy superconducting materials leads to a reduction in the level of hole-doping and the appearance of features typical of a pseudogap state even in samples with optimal oxygen content y ≈6.92.
the hole doping of YBa2Cu307 is determined by the structural perfection of the crystal lattice.
the structural disorder in fine-grained YBa2Cu 3Oy superconductor can be a factor that leads to a suppression of the hole doping and the appearance of features of the pseudogap phase.
